category_title: Female students who use silence as a mode of active listening
minimal_context: The student is participating in a Tuesday morning whole-class discussion on male power and privilege.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are having a classroom conversation on male power and privilege. I'd like to hear everyone's thoughts on this topic.

STUDENT: (Leans on her zipped-up backpack and remains silent while the boys start talking.)

TUTOR: I see the boys are talking and taking notes, but the girls are silent. Please share your thoughts.

STUDENT: (Continues to lean on her backpack, remaining silent in thoughtful contemplation rather than speaking out to the full class.)

TUTOR: ¡Mujeres! This is what I’m talking about! You don't need to feel you must be given permission by male teachers and peers to speak up.

STUDENT: We like to listen– Shut up, Alex! –we’re paying attention, but the guys are just talking back.

options.A: Maintaining a high ratio of praise statements to error correction statements (e.g., 3:1 to 10:1) during classroom conversations
options.B: Setting individual targets for improvement (guided by the tutor) which are monitored by the tutor, class teachers, and parents
options.C: Delivering a structured mindfulness program consisting of 12 hour-long sessions, generally twice-weekly over the course of the term
options.D: Learning to listen more judiciously and interrogating non-intersectional understandings of conscientización to more substantively attend to intersectionality
